Episodic vs Semantic — Select · Change · Reconstruct

Episodic memory captures autobiographical events tied to time and place; Semantic memory captures decontextualized facts and concepts. Both depend on medial temporal and neocortical systems and are reconstructive, not literal recordings. Episodic traces are vivid yet fragile; semantic knowledge is abstract yet durable. Episodic experiences sediment into semantic structure; semantic schemas guide what episodes are selected and how they are reconstructed.

The episodic–semantic distinction feeds the Select–Change–Reconstruct cycle; both are reconstructive and relational.
